system.cpu: 11th Gen Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-11850H @ 2.50GHz (8 cores, 16 threads)

method: hyperfine -N, 3 warmups (2 for compute-heavy); 30 runs for startup and fetch, 20 for compute-loop and serve, 10 for compute-heavy; wall time is mean ± σ. Each row is one hyperfine call with 0.0.6 listed first; startup and serve were repeated with 0.0.7 first to check order effects. Peak RSS is the largest PeakWorkingSetSize of 5 runs. Both versions are release builds measured in the same session; the machine was under other load, so σ is wide. 0.0.7 writes a run journal by default; --no-journal rows turn it off.

benchmarks.name: Startup and greeting
benchmarks.status: Loss vs 0.0.6 with the journal, +6.6 ms (+4.6 ms with 0.0.7 first); about 3 ms is creating the run directory and file and one sync, the rest is not profiled. Within noise with --no-journal. Win vs Node process start

benchmarks.name: Arithmetic loop (1M)
benchmarks.status: +7.5 ms vs 0.0.6, within σ; about the journal's startup cost. Win vs Node; Node startup dominates at this size

benchmarks.name: Arithmetic loop (50M)
benchmarks.status: Loss vs Node, 5.4x slower; QuickJS interprets bytecode and V8 compiles the loop. Within noise of 0.0.6
